    Ported from TauCeti (TauCeti.LinearAlgebra.BilinearForm.Basic, commit 580b6f9d5, Apache 2.0).

    Basic identities for bilinear forms #

    Away from characteristic two a bilinear form cannot be both symmetric and alternating without being zero: symmetry and alternation give B x y = B y x and B x y = -B y x, so 2 * B x y = 0, and cancelling the 2 leaves B x y = 0.

    That cancellation is all the hypothesis on the ring there is: 2 has to be regular, and nothing is asked of any other element, so the statement covers rings with zero divisors elsewhere. Over a field, or over any domain, IsRegular.of_ne_zero supplies the hypothesis from (2 : R) ≠ 0.

    For a left-separating alternating bilinear map on a module with a two-element basis, its value on that basis has trivial scalar annihilator. This holds over any commutative semiring and for maps valued in an arbitrary module.

    Main results #

    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.eq_zero_of_isSymm_of_isAlt: a symmetric alternating form over a ring in which 2 is regular is zero.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.nondegenerate_smul_iff: scalar multiplication by a regular element preserves nondegeneracy.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.nondegenerate_neg_iff: negating a bilinear form preserves nondegeneracy.
    • Module.Basis.dualBasis_smul_apply: the dual basis of a scalar multiple of a form.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.apply_add_self: polarization of a symmetric bilinear form.
    • LinearMap.IsAlt.eq_zero_of_smul_apply_basis_eq_zero: the value of a left-separating alternating bilinear map on a two-element basis has trivial scalar annihilator.

    theorem LinearMap.IsAlt.eq_zero_of_smul_apply_basis_eq_zero {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] [AddCommMonoid N] [Module R N] (b : Module.Basis (Fin 2) R M) {ω : M →ₗ[R] M →ₗ[R] N} (halt : ω.IsAlt) (hω : ω.SeparatingLeft) {r : R} (hr : r • (ω (b 0)) (b 1) = 0) :
    r = 0

    The value of a left-separating alternating bilinear map on a two-element basis has trivial scalar annihilator, over any commutative semiring.

    source
    theorem LinearMap.BilinForm.IsSymm.apply_add_self {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} (hB : B.IsSymm) (x y : M) :
    (B (x + y)) (x + y) = (B x) x + (B y) y + 2 * (B x) y

    Polarization of a symmetric bilinear form over a commutative semiring.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.eq_zero_of_isSymm_of_isAlt {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] (h2 : IsLeftRegular 2) {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} (hsymm : B.IsSymm) (halt : B.IsAlt) :
    B = 0

    Away from characteristic two a symmetric alternating form is zero: symmetry and alternation force 2 * B x y = 0, and a regular 2 cancels.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.nondegenerate_smul_iff {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommSemiring R] [AddCommMonoid M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} {c : R} (hc : IsRegular c) :
    (c • B).Nondegenerate ↔ B.Nondegenerate

    A scalar multiple of a bilinear form by a regular element is nondegenerate if and only if the original form is nondegenerate.

    source
    @[simp]
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.BilinForm.nondegenerate_neg_iff {R : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} [CommRing R] [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] {B : LinearMap.BilinForm R M} :
    (-B).Nondegenerate ↔ B.Nondegenerate

    Negating a bilinear form preserves nondegeneracy.

    @[simp]
    theorem Module.Basis.dualBasis_smul_apply {K : Type u_1} {V : Type u_2} {ι : Type u_3} [Field K] [AddCommGroup V] [Module K V] [Finite ι] [DecidableEq ι] (b : Basis ι K V) (B : LinearMap.BilinForm K V) (hB : B.Nondegenerate) (c : K) (hc : c ≠ 0) (i : ι) :
    ((c • B).dualBasis ⋯ b) i = c⁻¹ • (B.dualBasis hB b) i

    The basis dual to b for a nonzero scalar multiple c • B of a nondegenerate bilinear form is c⁻¹ times the basis dual to b for B.
